messages:
alex (support): FYI getting a bunch of customer tickets about slow responses on /v1/generate in us-west-2. p99 jumped to ~3.8s around 09:20 UTC. Model: rw-small-v1. SLO alert SLO-ALERT#4787 fired (p99 > 2s for 5m). Creating thread to coordinate mitigations.

oncall-bot: Alert SLO-ALERT#4787: service=inference region=us-west-2 metric=p99 latency value=3.8s window=5m :rotating_light:

jess (eng-runtime): copying quick notes — thanks Alex. First-pass triage: is the spike correlated with a deploy? any unusual error rates?

alex (support): no deploys recorded in the last hour. error rate steady, just tail latency. A couple of tickets include long prompts but many are short ones too.

kai (sre): pulling metrics now. looks like KV-cache miss rate jumped and sequence-length 90th->95th shift small. could be cache eviction churn. also see a bump in GPU scheduling wait for small instances.

maria (mlops): if it's cache churn, a quick mitigation is to enable reduced KV TTL to favor warm prefixes, or route a fraction to quantized fallback model to reduce per-token compute.

jess (eng-runtime): agreed. Propose immediate mitigations (ordered by low blast radius):
1) enable per-customer soft rate-limits for heavy callers (50 rps default)
2) enable fallback routing to rw-small-v1-quant for 20% of traffic in us-west-2
3) open circuit-breaker at p99=2.5s for 15m to force fast-fail for overloaded clients
4) increase min replicas in dedicated pool by +2 temporary
5) local prefix caching toggle (experimental) for 30m to reduce KV misses

Commands for quick actions (use infractl):
```bash
# enable circuit breaker
infractl set-circuit --service=inference --region=us-west-2 --p99=2.5s --open-for=15m --reason="p99 surge"

# enable fallback routing (20%)
infractl traffic-split --service=inference --region=us-west-2 --model=rw-small-v1-quant --weight=20

# temporary per-customer soft-limit
infractl set-rl --service=inference --region=us-west-2 --scope=per_customer --value=50rps

# increase min replicas
infractl scale --pool=inference-usw2-small --min=4
```

kai (sre): I'm running a slow query to check cache hit distribution and GPU queue times.

prod-signal-bot: metric-query: RUNNING "select percentile(latency_ms,99) by model,region from inference.metrics where time>now()-10m"

kai (sre): quick findings: p99 concentrated on rw-small-v1 only in us-west-2. rw-small-v1-quant p99=1.4s. GPU scheduling spikes align with heavy concurrent short requests (~200 concurrent).

alex (support): I've drafted a short customer message for affected folks offering temporary mitigation and ETA for update. ping me if we change routing so I can update tickets.

jess (eng-runtime): I'm flipping the fallback routing now to 20% and enabling the circuit breaker for 15m. Doing canary in 5% -> 20% over 90s.

maria (mlops): I'll watch model selection kernels — if kernel autoselect just regressed we might re-lock kernel affinity for rw-small-v1 to earlier profile. prepping a rollback patch.

(approx 2m later) jess (eng-runtime): fallback routing at 5% -> healthy -> scaling to 20%. infractl logs show no errors.

(approx 6m later) kai (sre): p99 dropped from 3.8s -> 1.9s in us-west-2 after routing + circuit breaker. KV miss rate down 30%. GPU queue reduced. Good sign.

alex (support): sending customers a note: "we've applied temporary routing and rate-limits to improve latency. We're monitoring and will follow up with timeline." :thumbsup:

jess (eng-runtime): next steps (owners):
- jess: keep fallback routing at 20% for 30m, watch error and quality regressions (QA dump for random sample).
- kai: verify circuit breaker logs & set alert for any automated throttles impacting paying customers.
- maria: finish kernel-affinity rollback if autotuner is to blame.
- alex: notify customers and update support queue.

kai (sre): long-term followups to include in postmortem:
- improve cache eviction (adaptive TTL by prefix popularity)
- SLO guardrail: add automatic fallback to quantized variant when p99>2s for 3m
- refine circuit-breaker hysteresis to avoid oscillation (open longer but with exponential backoff)
- add per-route cost/latency visibility in Console for rw-small-v1

maria (mlops): filing a ticket with kernel-autotune team to pin kernel selection for rw-small-v1 until we have confidence in new profiles.

jess (eng-runtime): summarizing now: immediate mitigations applied, p99 improved. we'll keep mitigations for 30m, then ramp down if stable. create postmortem if SLO recurrence within 24h.

alex (support): thanks team. I'll close the loop with customers and mark the support tickets as "mitigated - monitoring".

oncall-bot: Incident action log: SLO-ALERT#4787 -> mitigations executed: fallback-routing(20%), circuit-breaker(15m), per-customer-rl(50rps), scale-up(+2). status=monitoring.

jess (eng-runtime): leaving this thread open for 30m; ping me in thread for any regressions.

kai (sre): noted. If p99 creeps back up, fallback to region failover plan: reroute 40% -> us-east-1 after ops-review.

alex (support): last update to tickets sent at 09:55 UTC. status: monitoring. :white_check_mark:

(End of thread)
